subject: Midpoint OKR review & QBR prep: dependency decisions required
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Julianna Park <julianna@acme.com>, CloudOps Solutions <ops@cloudops.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Midpoint OKR review & QBR prep: dependency decisions required

Team —

We’re at the midpoint of the quarter and I want a concise reality check ahead of next week’s QBR prep slot. I attached a short deck (QBR_prep_deck_v1.pdf) and an initial dependency matrix. High level:

1) Objective A (Serving runtime throughput) — behind by ~25% on throughput targets; root cause is backend batching rollout and a blocked CloudOps quota increase.
2) Objective B (Cost optimization/Reductions) — on track for model selection milestones but latency regressions risk the metric.
3) Objective C (Enterprise Expansion) — pipeline healthy; Acme POC needs dedicated SLA decisions by 7/28 to keep contract timeline.

Asks (please action or assign owners):
- CloudOps quota increase (URGENT) — we need a decision and ETA from CloudOps by EOD Tue 7/20. Linking CloudOps in thread to avoid context switch.
- Can the runtime team accept a temporary re-scope: reduce the default batch window from 60ms to 40ms for low-latency routes to avoid user-visible regressions? If so, what is the estimated impact on cost and ops complexity?
- Laura / Monica: confirm whether we can push one non-core mid-cycle feature to next quarter (the adaptive cache TTL experiment) to free 0.5 FTE of engineering runway.
- Vivek: please list the minimal infra commits you need from the tools team to hit Objective A SLOs; add to the dependency matrix.

Please reply with clear yes/no/ETA on the three bullets above. For QBR prep I want a single-slide summary per objective by 7/23 COB. I’m keeping the agenda tight: status, risks, mitigation ask, and top 2 decision points.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, Julianna Park <julianna@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint OKR review & QBR prep: dependency decisions required

Rishi —

Quick responses inline:

- CloudOps quota increase: I’ve pinged our CloudOps contact and copied ops@cloudops.com. They asked for projected peak GPU hours; Monica, can you confirm numbers by EOD? If we can provide that, ops said they can prioritise the quota change and may give a provisional increase within 48 hours.

- Re-scope batch window: short answer: yes, we can roll a shorter default batch window for latency-sensitive routes, but it will increase per-token cost by an estimated 8–12% while we stabilize. We should make this a targeted flag (route-level) rather than global. Vivek — can you confirm if we can toggle that via existing config rollout by 7/22?

- Push adaptive cache TTL experiment: I support pushing it out one quarter. We can free a behavioral-data engineer 0.4–0.6 FTE depending on whether we can pause sampling. Monica — thoughts?

I’ll draft the objective slides tonight and share a first pass in the drive link.

Laura
Director, Product Management
--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-20T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint OKR review & QBR prep: dependency decisions required

Rishi / team —

I updated the dependency_matrix.csv and attached it to this thread. Short version:

- Quota increase ask: we need a sustained bump of +40% GPU hours for two weeks to validate the batching rollout. If CloudOps can grant a 14-day provisional increase we will run the larger-scale test and provide telemetry to justify a longer-term commit. Ops, can you confirm if you prefer a specific window?

- Batch window re-scope: we can implement a route-level flag and toggle it during peak hours. Engineering estimate: 3 engineer-weeks to implement the flag, 1 week QA, then staged rollout. Cost delta: ~+10% per-token on affected traffic. If we accept this trade-off now, we can preserve customer experience while we continue to optimize batching algorithms.

- Minimal infra commits: 1) temporary autoscale rule loosen (already in progress), 2) short-term increase to preemptive cache nodes (2 nodes), 3) permission change for the runtime team to trigger soft-restarts (controlled role). I added these to dependency_matrix.csv with owners.

Action items assigned in the matrix; I’ll incorporate any timing changes you provide.

Vivek
SVP, Engineering
--

Date: 2026-07-21T13:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint OKR review & QBR prep: dependency decisions required

Rishi / Redwood team —

Thanks for the transparency and the clear asks. From Acme’s side:

- SLA decision: we can agree to the dedicated SLA outline you proposed, but we need the final wording by 7/27. Our legal team wants a one-week review window prior to signature.
- Quota window: the provisional 14-day bump is fine; we prefer the window to start 7/29. That gives our infra team time to align schedules.
- Batch window tradeoff: Acme prefers that any temporary latency/throughput tradeoffs be limited to non-production feature flags; if the route-level flag impacts the main inference endpoints we need a mitigation plan (circuit-breaker thresholds, detailed rollback playbook).

I’ll review the QBR slide Laura uploads and give feedback by 7/24. Monica, I’m happy to sync on the sampling pause—we can likely accept a temporary reduction in experimental telemetry for the pilot.

– Julianna
Sr. Director, Product Engineering
Acme Corp
